cards: Homer is the ancient Greek poet to whom the Iliad and the Odyssey are attributed, epic poems probably composed in the 8th or 7th century BCE from a long oral tradition.
Sargon II was a king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire in the late eighth century BCE, who founded a new capital at Dur-Sharrukin.
Hesiod was a Greek poet of around 700 BCE who lived at Ascra in Boeotia, where his father had settled after leaving Cyme in Aeolis.
Isaiah was a Hebrew prophet active in Jerusalem in the later 8th century BCE, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah.
Tiglath-pileser III was king of Assyria from 745 to 727 BCE and the architect of the Neo-Assyrian imperial system.
Hezekiah was king of Judah from about 715 to 686 BCE, remembered in the Hebrew Bible as a reformer who centralised worship in Jerusalem.
r. c. 715–686 BCE · Ancient Near East
Hosea was a Hebrew prophet in the northern Kingdom of Israel in the 8th century BCE, during its last decades before the Assyrian conquest.
Ahaz was king of Judah in the second half of the 8th century BCE.
Argishti I was king of Urartu from about 786 to 764 BCE, the son and successor of Menua.
r. c. 786–764 BCE · Ancient Near East
King Ping of Zhou was the first king of the Eastern Zhou, reigning from 770 to 720 BCE.
King Wu of Chu, personal name Xiong Tong, ruled the State of Chu from 740 to 690 BCE.
Bao Si was a consort of King You of Zhou in the 8th century BCE.
Rezin was the last king of Aram-Damascus, reigning in the mid-8th century BCE.
Rusa I was king of Urartu in the later 8th century BCE, ruling from about 735 to 714 BCE.
r. c. 735–714 BCE · Ancient Near East
Shabaka was a king of Kush and pharaoh of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, who ruled in the late 8th century BCE.
d. c. 705 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Shalmaneser V was king of Assyria from 727 to 722 BCE, son and successor of Tiglath-Pileser III.
Hoshea was the last king of Israel, reigning from about 732 to 722 BCE.
r. c. 732–722 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jehoash, or Joash, was king of Israel in the early eighth century BCE, the grandson of Jehu.
r. c. 798–782 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jeroboam II was king of Israel in the first half of the eighth century BCE, reigning about forty years according to the Books of Kings.
r. c. 786–746 BCE · Ancient Near East
Menahem was king of Israel from about 752 to 742 BCE.
r. c. 752–742 BCE · Ancient Near East
Midas was a king of Phrygia in the late 8th century BCE, ruling from Gordion.
Pekah was king of Israel from about 740 to 732 BCE, an army officer who seized the throne by killing Pekahiah.
r. c. 740–732 BCE · Ancient Near East
Pekahiah was king of Israel for about two years around 742–740 BCE, succeeding his father Menahem.
r. c. 742–740 BCE · Ancient Near East
King You of Zhou was the last king of the Western Zhou dynasty, reigning from 781 to 771 BCE.
Merodach-baladan II (Marduk-apla-iddina II) was a Chaldean chief of Bit-Yakin who seized the throne of Babylon in 721 BCE with Elamite support and held it until Sargon II of Assyria drove him out in…
Nabu-mukin-zeri was a chief of the Chaldean tribe of Bit-Amukani who seized the throne of Babylon in 731 BCE after a period of turmoil following the death of Nabonassar.
Ambaris was a king of Bit-Burutash in Tabal in south-central Anatolia in the late 8th century BCE.
Amenirdis I was a Kushite princess, daughter of King Kashta and sister of Piye and Shabaka, who served as God's Wife of Amun at Thebes in the late 8th century BCE.
Amos was a Hebrew prophet of the 8th century BCE, a herdsman from Tekoa in Judah who preached in the northern Kingdom of Israel under Jeroboam II.
Bakenranef, called Bocchoris by the Greeks, was the second and last king of the Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Sais in the western Delta in the 720s BCE.
d. c. 720 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Duke Zhuang of Zheng (reigned 743–701 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Zheng who made it the leading state of the early Spring and Autumn period.
Iranzu was a king of Mannaea, south of Lake Urmia in north-western Iran, in the late 8th century BCE.
Iuput II was a king in the Nile Delta in the late 8th century BCE, usually located at Leontopolis and assigned to the Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt.
Osorkon III was a king of the Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt, a Libyan line that ruled parts of Upper Egypt alongside the Bubastite kings.
r. c. 787–759 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Rudamun was the last king of the Theban line known as the Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt, reigning briefly in the 8th century BCE.
Shepenupet I was a daughter of Osorkon III and God's Wife of Amun at Thebes in the 8th century BCE, the first holder of the office to wield wide political power.
Takelot III was an Egyptian pharaoh of the 8th century BCE, a son of Osorkon III, who first served as High Priest of Amun at Thebes and then as co-ruler with his father.
Tarhunazi was the last king of Melid, a Neo-Hittite kingdom at Arslantepe near Malatya in eastern Turkey.
Wasusarma was a king of Tabal in south-central Anatolia in the 8th century BCE, son of Tuwati.
fl. c. 730 BCE · Ancient Near East
Adad-nirari III was king of Assyria from about 811 to 783 BCE, succeeding his father Shamshi-Adad V while young, possibly under the influence of his mother Sammuramat.
